system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels have no contractual effect and should be disregarded. Several positions are materially adverse to the Buyer and inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free acquisition.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher cap—open at **50%**, with a fallback no lower than **30%**—and separate regimes for title, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and adjustments. | **Reject 20% as the complete liability package; counter at 50% with appropriate carve-outs**, because a AUD 4.8m ceiling may not adequately protect a buyer paying AUD 24m for the entire business. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, so only the excess is recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims, and a **tipping basket**; suggested AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 aggregate basket. | **Counter with a AUD 10k de minimis and AUD 100k tipping basket**, because the proposed thresholds could exclude numerous recurring or related losses and leave the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250k. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire **18 months after Completion**; Seller seeks limitations to apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer periods for tax, title, IP, covenants and specific indemnities; timely notice should preserve a claim until finally resolved. | **Extend general survival to 24 months and expressly separate other claim periods**, because 18 months may expire before a second audit cycle reveals historical issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month period as general warranties. | Title, capacity and authority claims capped at **100% of the purchase price**, surviving for the applicable statutory limitation period—preferably seven years. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental warranties**, because the Buyer must have full recourse if the Seller lacked title or authority to sell the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud carve-out; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions purport to cover all Claims. | Express disapplication of every cap, threshold, time bar, disclosure, knowledge, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy restriction for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment. | **Insert a comprehensive, uncapped fraud carve-out**, because the Seller must not benefit from limitations where it or its relevant officers or agents acted dishonestly. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify their nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable consequences; referenced documents should be precisely identified. | **Delete blanket data-room and public-record disclosure**, because bulk disclosure shifts the diligence risk to the Buyer without establishing that a warranty exception was fairly explained. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Preferably no knowledge bar; alternatively, only the actual knowledge of a short list of named Buyer personnel, without constructive knowledge, adviser attribution or duty of inquiry. | **Reject “discoverable” and adviser-imputed knowledge**, because it converts disclosure and warranty protection into an unreasonable constructive-knowledge test. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller gives reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, apparently irrespective of clause 11.3 conditions. No final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists. | A genuine condition precedent requiring final, effective and preferably unconditional consent, satisfaction of all associated conditions, no adverse amendment or fee, and Buyer approval of any conditions; waiver only by Buyer. | **Do not complete until the Bluefen consent and all conditions are effective and acceptable to Buyer**, because Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release is to be provided **after Completion**. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller proceeds and simultaneous delivery of irrevocable releases and discharges of all Company and asset security, guarantees and liabilities. | **Make repayment and release a Completion deliverable, not a post-Completion promise**, because the agreed transaction is debt-free/cash-free and the Buyer should not acquire secured debt exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are said to be the Seller’s matter but are omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unresolved. | Seller to fund or bear the full bonuses and all on-costs, with the amount treated as debt-like/leakage or deducted from Seller proceeds and expressly included in funds flow. | **Add the bonuses and all payroll-related on-costs to Completion funds flow**, because the liability is triggered by the sale and may otherwise remain in the acquired Company. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains open and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Payment before Completion, evidence of cleared funds and effective transfer/confirmation of all SOW3 Project Materials, backed by a specific indemnity covering all resulting losses and IP defects. | **Require payment and confirmed IP transfer as a Completion condition plus a broad specific indemnity**, because reimbursing only the fee does not cure defective ownership of a core business asset. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unresolved. | Pre-Completion forensic investigation, preservation and remediation, required regulator/data-subject notifications, continuing update obligations, and a specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident losses. | **Require investigation results and a standalone privacy/cyber indemnity outside general thresholds**, because potential exposure involving approximately 1,240 records cannot presently be quantified or fairly treated as immaterial. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD 330,000 aggregate—are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Evidence of terms, timing, termination rights, accrual and benefit period; Seller bears pre-Completion or transaction-accelerated amounts, with post-Completion benefit properly reflected in working capital. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without diligence and price allocation**, because the Disclosure Letter itself does not establish whether the commitments are avoidable, accrued or attributable to the post-Completion period. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature unless expressly excluded. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, leakage, debt and purchase-price adjustments, fraud and equitable relief. | **Expressly ring-fence each claim category from the general limitations**, because an omnibus limitation could unintentionally defeat negotiated dollar-for-dollar and Completion protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence that it holds 100% of the shares. | Independent ASIC and PPSR checks, original share certificates or loss declarations, executed transfers, confirmation of issued capital/options and beneficial ownership, lien releases, board approvals and full title warranties. | **Treat the register as evidence, not a substitute for verification and Completion documents**, because it does not alone establish clean beneficial title, absence of encumbrances or valid authority to transfer. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general 20%/18-month warranty regime. | A standalone pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with seven-year survival and up to 100% recourse; enhanced IP warranties and indemnities with a higher cap and longer survival appropriate to a technology business. | **Reopen and separately negotiate tax and IP protections**, because historical tax liabilities and ownership/infringement of core analytics IP are not ordinary short-tail warranty risks. |

**Priority Completion blockers:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment and security releases, Ironquay payment/IP transfer, and proper treatment of the employee bonuses. The privacy incident should also be investigated and specifically indemnified before the Buyer commits to complete.
=== END ADVICE ===
